title: Use of "run" as a noun is confusing

labels.name: editorial
labels.description: Changes that do not affect how the standard is understood

body:
There are multiple places in the spec where the noun "run" is used to mean "sequence", particularly in the context of a "run of content". Given that more commonly in the spec, "run" is used as a verb describing an operation or algorithm, it would be clearer if a different term was used to describe the noun unrelated to the verb.

Here's a particularly confusing example:

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#paragraphs

> Let view be a view of the DOM that replaces all a, ins, del, and map elements in the document with their contents\. Then, in view, for each run of sibling phrasing content nodes uninterrupted by other types of content, in an element that accepts content other than phrasing content as well as phrasing content, let first be the first node of the run, and let last be the last node of the run\. For each such run that consists of at least one node that is neither embedded content nor inter\-element whitespace, a paragraph exists in the original DOM from immediately before first to immediately after last\. \(Paragraphs can thus span across a, ins, del, and map elements\.\)

And here it is again using "sequence" instead:

> Let view be a view of the DOM that replaces all a, ins, del, and map elements in the document with their contents\. Then, in view, for each sequence of sibling phrasing content nodes uninterrupted by other types of content, in an element that accepts content other than phrasing content as well as phrasing content, let first be the first node of the sequence, and let last be the last node of the sequence\. For each such sequence that consists of at least one node that is neither embedded content nor inter\-element whitespace, a paragraph exists in the original DOM from immediately before first to immediately after last\. \(Paragraphs can thus span across a, ins, del, and map elements\.\)
